title: Research audit: compact interior carries and exact exceptional repair (no new kappa)
body:
The compact-control source-load can restore every temporary and still flip the wrong target bit when a carry reaches another digit. This **research note / adversarial mathematical audit** proves the exact guarded later-source law: selected bit i flips by c_i XOR the incoming compact carry. Only interior carries matter; the final outgoing carry is harmless. Consequently the highest u digit need not be excluded by the sufficient saturation guard.

The existing guarded construction is correct. The relaxed predicate stays inside this standalone audit. **No new kappa, supplier, or fixed-tape runtime claim.** All additions are confined to `research/compact-carry-repair-audit/`; production sources, `upstream/`, and the selected frontier are unchanged.

The package includes the universal integer argument, independent interpreter, source pins and deterministic evidence. Its two-digit counterexample `(x,y,t,u,b)=(16,4224,0,1,2)` gives y=4752 instead of 4240 while all scratch restores. Within the tested later-source rectangle the expanded good set grows from 16,384 to 32,768 representatives. Sorted-hole checks verify unique record identities, and a real wrong-key `T(q)` mutation fills every one of 32,256 holes while misplacing all 32,256 records.

Reproduce with Python 3.11+ and its standard library:

```sh
python3 -B research/compact-carry-repair-audit/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_COMPACT_CARRY_REPAIR_AUDIT: 1310720 representatives; 3072 source comparisons; 7 negative controls`.

The exhaustive interpreter checks both source orders, arbitrary active dirty fields, original and expanded exceptional sets, sorted repair, and a materialized highest-bit XOR. The proof justifies spectator lifting to two particular complete 2^36-address rectangles; those addresses were not individually enumerated. Production-source comparisons are sampled separately, not described as exhaustive. Seven controls isolate three guard failures, reversed repair order, wrong/duplicate destination keys and omitted highest XOR. Exact density checks include unclipped bounds.

Validation passed: default and optimized-Python receipt replays; an isolated clean dependency export from an unrelated working directory; deliberate source-drift rejection; 17 relevant compact-control tests; `make selected-record-check`; whitespace checks. Full `make verify`, the selected supplier cold replay, and remote CI success are not claimed. Uniform recursion, complete field availability, physical hosting, precision, tape costs and analytic transfer remain inherited obligations.

Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`; assignment seed 69. Accepted conditional kappa remains 51110230636731/31250000000000000. No pinned coordination issue exists, so the claim is local. A refreshed 576-PR queue found concurrent #735 (`8d36139e49add1e55795e283b3bfa45e1cfe1bf0`): Aryan Sudhir audits the original eight-rotation wide-slot primitive, while this audits the different compact-control primitive. No #735 code or result is consumed.

Credit Douglas Colkitt's compact-control construction and tests, OpenAI's original manuscript, Aryan Sudhir's distinct concurrent audit, and the selected checkpoint's cumulative contributors. Contribution by John-Michael Smith / @jp3isme, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, code, writing and scoped agent review.
